correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, only intra-part vertex pairs have distance two and their common neighborhood is exactly the outside of that part. Hence feasible complements avoid containment in each non-singleton class. Inclusion-exclusion has just one common multi-family intersection; minimal complements are precisely singleton vertices or cross-class pairs. With no singleton parts the faces form the independence complex of the dual rank-two partition matroid; shellability plus Euler evaluation gives a wedge of a-1 spheres in dimension N-3. With singleton parts an exact union of two cones suspends the previous complex b times. Cases a=0,1 are contractible. The independent finite program checks 88 profiles, 10,764 subsets, 804 facets, 5,200 basis-exchange instances and mod-two homology of 64 cases. Its finite checks are not treated as an unrestricted or integral proof.

originality.rationale: The 2025 general distance-two criterion and the 2023 two-cut results are explicitly recognized as theorems strong enough to cover the basic feasibility condition and the pure no-singleton topological case, respectively. Balanced complete bipartite visibility polynomials are explicitly prior. The assessed combination instead gives a unified exact labelled face/facet enumeration, canonical matroidality boundary, and nonpure but integral single-dimension sphere-wedge homotopy classification in complete multipartite graphs with singleton parts. Source inspections and semantic searches found no explicit theorem or directly stated stronger specialized result covering that combined conclusion. Residual priority risk remains because the main proof employs well-known general constructions.
residual_risks: A broader published distance-two criterion, an existing two-cut-complex framework, and a general suspension theorem together make important components derivable; priority of the entire specific combination is provisional.
The known balanced complete bipartite polynomial and pure base topology are subsumed prior results, not original claims.
Database retrieval and inspected full-text sections cannot rule out unindexed equivalent results or unpublished specialized computations.
Independent mathematical audit is not performed.

value.rationale: The result determines the entire natural family of total mutual-visibility complexes for arbitrary multipartite part-size profiles: two complete cardinality polynomials, a sharp matroidality/purity dichotomy and the integral homotopy type. Mixed singleton and non-singleton profiles are nonpure, yet have reduced integral homology exclusively in a dimension one below the maximal facet dimension with sphere multiplicity a-1 independent of individual class sizes. This structural contrast is motivated by how adding universal singleton vertices changes shortest-path constraints, and is not merely a scalar extremal increment or arbitrary fixed finite slice.
